change: CAPSTONE_LEVEL0_SHRINK is on by default: level0, the heap every application port links unless it asks for another, now narrows each returned pointer to the bytes requested. -DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_SHRINK=0 restores the old behaviour and is what the heap qualification's control needs.
what_it_does_not_give: temporal safety. free still only marks the block free, so a stale pointer keeps working and reads whatever occupies the memory next. That is sublet_heap.c's job and is unchanged here.
prior_state: the switch has existed since 2026-09-23 (5e7157e20bb0, 'per-object heap bounds (opt-in)') and was defined nowhere: no build, no gate, no port turned it on. The threads lane's 'Qualify level0 shrink across the application and libc gates' (92d21b84) is a different shrink -- realloc releasing an unused tail (7795986d) -- and did not bound objects.

matched_pair.method: one contract source, two images: the default (bounds) and -DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_SHRINK=0 (the control). Run through application-supervisor, which is what run-heap.py uses.
matched_pair.reading: the protection fires on both size classes and the control misses both, so the check is meaningful and the legitimate heap paths are unaffected

regression.application_gate: run.py --repeat 1 on the bounds image: 25 PASS, 0 FAIL
regression.gate_caveat: the gate's perl.dom and mruby.dom come from the #144 kit and were built against the unbounded heap, so the gate proves the contract image, not those two ports

mruby.per_test: 1609 tests compared one by one, 0 differ
mruby.reading: a real interpreter whose every malloc is now bounded passes its own suite exactly as it does natively

consequence_for_the_heap_qualification: run-heap.py hard-codes level0 as the unprotected control (control = label == 'level0' and mode in FAULTS, then 'control faulted' must not fire). With bounds on by default that control must be built with -DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_SHRINK=0, or its two bounds cases fault on both arms and the gate fails. applications.md now says so and names the control image contract-noshrink.dom.
not_measured: libc-test has not been re-run against the bounded heap
no port other than mruby was rebuilt against it; Perl, CPython, SQLite, FFmpeg and tshark are untouched here

silicon: level0.c already records that a narrowed capability of 4 KiB or more, stored and reloaded, is rounded outward to its representable granule because block bases are only 16-aligned. capstone-qemu keeps full precision, so this measurement does not see it, and a large object's bounds on the board may be wider than the request
